value.body: Law graduates can work in research, policy and legal writing instead of litigation or corporate practice — as law clerks assisting judges, researchers at think tanks and law-reform bodies, editors at legal publishers and databases, or policy staff in government projects and NGOs.

items.label: Supreme Court law clerks
items.note: ~90 posts in the 2026-27 cycle; contract term
items.source: Supreme Court of India notification (as reported)

items.label: Clerkship remuneration
items.source: Supreme Court of India notification (as reported)

items.label: Other employers
items.value: High Courts, think tanks, legal publishers, law-reform and policy bodies

value.title: How you get in
value.body: An LLB from a Bar Council of India–recognised institution (final-year students can apply for some clerkships). Supreme Court and High Court clerkships use written tests and interviews; think tanks and publishers hire through applications, writing samples and interviews.

value.title: At a glance
items: Clerkships are short contracts but give close exposure to judicial work.
Strong research and writing samples matter more than grades for think-tank roles.
Many people later move into litigation, academia, an LLM or public-policy roles.
